title: A spectacular museum
text: The National Art Museum of Catalonia (MNAC) (in Catalan: National Art Museum of Catalonia is one of the main cultural spaces in Barcelona and Spain. It is installed in the imposing National Palace of Montjuïc (Palau Nacional), on the Montjuïc hill, with a view of Plaça d'Espanya. The little path from the square to the museum is already a spectacle of appreciation of Beauty!  The current museum was founded in 1990, uniting the old Museum of Art of Catalonia (from 1934) and the Museum of Modern Art (from 1945), in addition to incorporating other collections. author: Clebicar

title: Well worth your money, probably worth your time
text:
- Worth the visit just for the view and looking on the outside of the building
- Very nice relaxing view over the gardens from the roof
- The Romanesk era can be quickly walked through. A lot of very same:y paintings. 
- Renaissance and Gothic era was quite good. 
- The "modern" era is a bit misleading, it's like 1850 and forward (in a good way because most modern art is sh*t). They have some Gaudi furniture inside. 
- Overall, well worth the €12. I think the receptionist said something about the ticket being valid for 2 days, but unless you live very closeby it's better to just take it all in

title: Exit the metro at Pl. d'Espagne and go up the escalators; magnificent photos to be taken from the bottom.

author: Olivier61M

title: Definitely visit if you have time
text: This was one of my favorite things we did while in Barcelona. Easy subway ride in and just a gorgeous area to walk around in. The museum is beautiful and with very unique and old art that I've never experienced in the USA. The cafe inside was surprisingly good and cheap too! Highly recommend.

title: Terrific art museum with some outstanding Romanesque art
text: This museum houses an amazing collection of medieval church frescos that look Byzantine to my uneducated eye - which have been reassembled from their original locations and displayed in a way that lets you experience how they originally appeared inside churches that are no longer extant. I am not Christian but can still appreciate the artistry and devotion represented in these works. Also a tremendous collection of modern Catalonian art. I am not really an art buff nor is my partner but we spent hours wandering through this museum and would call it a must-see in a city full of amazing sites.
author: TonyFio67

title: Romanesque muralism and more in Montjuic
text:
The National Art Museum of Catalonia (MNAC) is one of the
most relevant museum institutions in the world, not only for the
monumentality of its headquarters, but for housing the collection of mural
painting that is the most complete and important Romanesque one on the planet.

The history of the MNAC is inextricably linked to the Palau Nacional,
the majestic neo-baroque building that dominates the mountain of Montjuic,
designed as the great central pavilion of the International Exposition
of Barcelona of 1929.

title: A Perfect Day at MNAC and the Magic Fountain
text:
Visiting the National Art Museum of Catalonia (MNAC) was one of the highlights of my time in Barcelona. The museum is housed in a magnificent building, and the panoramic views of the city from the entrance are absolutely stunning.
I enjoyed exploring the museum at my own pace, taking time to appreciate its impressive collection of Romanesque frescoes, Gothic art, Renaissance and Baroque masterpieces, as well as modern Catalan works. 
MNAC is well worth a visit. I highly recommend choosing the self-guided option if you prefer the flexibility to spend more time with the collections that interest
